topics.label: Lecture introduction and framing
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the lecture topic and sets expectations regarding the importance and complexity of the complement system.

topics.label: Fundamentals and core concepts of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics provide an overview of complement biology, clarify historical naming conventions, and establish C3 as the central molecule of the cascade.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the three biochemical recognition pathways that generate C3 convertases and establish the local threshold for complement activation.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the downstream immune effector functions executed upon complement activation, including phagocytic opsonization, inflammation, and membrane lysis.

topics.label: Host regulation and self-protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory factors and mechanisms that prevent complement activation from damaging host tissues.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores the specific pathological presentations and clinical diseases resulting from deficiencies in various complement components.

topics.label: Microbial evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the evolutionary strategies used by pathogens, particularly Staphylococcus aureus, to evade and neutralize complement defenses.

topics.label: Lecture wrap-up and next session preview
topics.groupedBecause: This closing subtopic concludes the lecture on complement and previews the upcoming session on the adaptive immune system.
